notes: Core architecture and final Windows host smoke are PASS. A real Windows VS Code Claude Code 2.1.243 session received PackRat-owned queued requests through the documented Stop-hook continuation path and continued in the same conversation, including repeated exact-text round trips. Auto Queue is intentionally not an immediate send action: after one-time Connect, the user sends one normal Claude message so the supported UserPromptSubmit hook identifies the active chat; Queue Prompt then saves a follow-up locally while Claude is working; the saved prompt is supplied as the next request only after the current turn finishes. Normal session UI uses a short preview of the latest real user prompt and keeps exact session identifiers in advanced diagnostics only. The installer bundles ready-made profiles for five Stream Deck families. PackRat stores queued prompts locally, preserves existing Claude settings and third-party hooks, never reads Claude credentials, and does not claim external control of Claude Code's private native queued-message UI. Hook integration uses a per-install authenticated localhost endpoint, fail-safe session targeting, a six-continuation safety cap, a 9,000-character queue prompt ceiling, locked dependencies, and direct discovery of native Windows Claude Code plus the CLI bundled with VS Code and common VS Code forks. Canonical Rat Ship routes registered Stream Deck plugins through official Elgato validation and packaging, deterministic product art, resilient local Maker Console automation, and an explicit monetization guard.
